text.en: Asha folded a paper to make a triangle and then a rectangle. "Shapes follow rules," said her teacher.

Two lines cut by a transversal make pairs of angles: corresponding, alternate and co-interior. The angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees and its exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles. Congruent triangles are of the same shape and size and are proved by the SSS, SAS, ASA and RHS rules.
A quadrilateral has four sides, and its angles add up to 360 degrees. Special types are the parallelogram, rectangle, rhombus, square, trapezium and kite. In a parallelogram, opposite sides and opposite angles are equal and the diagonals bisect each other.
A circle has parts such as the centre, radius, chord, diameter, arc and segment. The perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects the chord, equal chords subtend equal angles at the centre, and a cyclic quadrilateral has opposite angles that add up to 180 degrees. Practical geometry constructs these figures with a ruler and compass.

Draw a line across two parallel lines. Corresponding angles occupy the same corner position where the transversal crosses each line. In this setting, they have equal measures.
Alternate interior angles lie between the two parallel lines, on opposite sides of the transversal. Co-interior angles lie on the same side and their measures add to one hundred eighty degrees.
If one interior angle is sixty-eight degrees, its co-interior partner is one hundred twelve degrees. A matching alternate interior angle is sixty-eight degrees.

Extend a side of a triangle to make an exterior angle. The exterior angle and its adjacent interior angle form a straight line. This makes the exterior angle equal to the other two interior angles added together.

board.text: Exterior angle = two opposite interior angles added

text.en: In a triangle with remote interior angles forty and seventy degrees, the exterior angle is one hundred ten degrees. Its adjacent interior angle is seventy degrees.
For side-angle-side congruence, the given angle must be between the two given sides. Match the vertices before writing which two triangles are congruent.
Join opposite vertices of a simple convex quadrilateral. A diagonal creates two triangles. Their two angle sums together account for one full turn of interior angles.
A parallelogram has both pairs of opposite sides parallel. Follow one diagonal across the parallel lines to find equal alternate angles in the resulting triangles.
At the intersection of a parallelogram’s diagonals, each diagonal divides into two equal parts. If the whole first diagonal is fourteen centimetres, each of its halves is seven centimetres.
A rectangle adds four right angles to the properties of a parallelogram. A rhombus adds four equal sides. A square has both sets of properties.

board.text: Square: four equal sides and four right angles

text.en: A chord joins two points on the circle. A diameter is a chord through the centre. The diameter is the longest chord because it is twice the radius.
Two radii enclose a sector with the arc between them. A chord and an arc bound a segment. Compare the straight boundaries in the two figures.

board.text: Sector: two radii and an arc

text.en: Draw a perpendicular from a circle’s centre to a chord. Connect the centre to both ends of the chord with radii. The resulting right triangles have equal hypotenuses and share one leg.

board.text: Equal radii plus common leg → congruent right triangles

text.en: The two segments of that chord are therefore equal. If a chord is twelve centimetres long, the perpendicular from the centre meets it six centimetres from either end.
A central angle is measured at the centre of the circle. An angle at the circumference standing on the same arc has half that measure.

board.text: Central angle = 2 × angle on the same arc

text.en: A diameter subtends a half turn at the centre. An angle at the circumference that stands on the diameter is half of one hundred eighty degrees, which is a right angle.
When four vertices lie on one circle, the two arcs used by opposite angles make a full turn together. Each opposite angle is half the measure of its own arc.

board.text: Cyclic quadrilateral: opposite angles sum to 180°

text.en: If one angle of a cyclic quadrilateral is ninety-five degrees, subtract from one hundred eighty to find its opposite angle. The difference is eighty-five degrees.
In a construction, connect a vertex to the midpoint of its opposite side to draw a median. Two medians meet at the centroid, and the third passes through the same point.
Perpendicular bisectors go through side midpoints at right angles. Their meeting point is the circumcentre, which is the same distance from all three vertices.
Angle bisectors meet at the incentre. It is equally far from the three sides, so that distance gives the radius of the circle that fits inside the triangle and touches all three sides.
An altitude is a perpendicular from a vertex to the line through the opposite side. The altitudes meet at the orthocentre, which can be outside an obtuse triangle.

problem.en: A circle has radius 10 cm and a chord 12 cm long. How far is the chord from the centre?

text.en: Draw a perpendicular from the centre to the chord. It divides the chord into two pieces of six centimetres.

why.en: A perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord.

text.en: Use one radius of ten centimetres as the hypotenuse of a right triangle, with one leg of six centimetres.

why.en: Ten squared minus six squared is sixty-four, so the other leg is eight centimetres.

prompt.en: A friend says The angles of a quadrilateral add up to 180 degrees. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: A triangle's angles add up to 180.

points.en: Perpendicular from the centre bisects a chord.
Cyclic quadrilateral opposite angles sum to 180.
